keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1830-1900: the Tooro province. The page gives no area or boundary; the Bunyoro page calls Tooro 'the large province' that 'separated' in the 1830s 'claiming much of the lucrative salt works'. The ledger takes the land back to Bunyoro in 1880 and returns it in 1891.

ledger.note: 1880: Tooro reverts to Bunyoro. The reign list has 'Interregnum, reverted to Bunyoro: 1880-1891'; the text says 'Absorbed into Bunyoro-Kitara in 1876', the year the list's last kings begin to be short-lived. [Reviewer af-05, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 to 2: the page's text has 1876 and its reign list 1880.]

ledger.note: 1900: Tooro signs its treaty with the British. 'The British signed a treaty with Toro in 1900, described as much less generous than the Buganda terms' (Uganda Protectorate page); the page gives no day or the clauses, so the year is the page's and the loss of sovereignty is the researcher's reading.

sources.title: Toro Kingdom
sources.note: Founded 1830 by Olimi I; absorbed into Bunyoro 1876; interregnum reverted to Bunyoro 1880-1891; independence reasserted 1891; reign list; abolished 1967, reinstated 1993.

notes:
New state (Cliopatria has no Toro row). Two pages: Toro Kingdom and, for 1900, Uganda Protectorate; the Bunyoro page (opened for the Bunyoro dossier) dates the secession to the 1830s.

Disagreements: founded 1830 (text) or Olimi I reigning from 1822 (list); absorbed into Bunyoro 1876 (text) or reverted 1880 (list). The dossier takes 1830 and 1880. Not on the page: the 1891 Lugard treaty, Kasagama's restoration, the protectorate declaration for Tooro, the Rwenzururu movement, wars with Bunyoro, any territory or area. The end year 1900 is the treaty year of the Uganda Protectorate page; the 1894 protectorate may have reached Tooro earlier.
